source_snapshot.procedure: Enable SNMP in BMC WebUI and inspect displayed information.
source_snapshot.criteria: SNMP v1/v3 functions normally and information displays correctly.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL but proposes SNMPv2c GET rather than trap capture.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED for version mismatch, receiver, stimulus, expected payload and cleanup.

old_problem: The prior review correctly rejected v2c GET as trap evidence, but left the case pending instead of binding the vendor-specific OID/event values as Project Configuration around the standards-defined v1 and v3 notification flows.
disposition_reason: The title fixes the tested object as asynchronous trap delivery, and Criteria explicitly requires v1 and v3. Standards define their wire and security behavior; the project MIB, safe test event, receiver and credentials supply platform values. The two modes must be executed and reported separately, and an SNMP GET remains only optional reachability evidence.
decision_basis: Direct review covered XLSX row 749, its DeepSeek columns, exact GPT V2 object and historical record.
RFC 1157 defines the v1 Trap-PDU and receiver behavior; RFC 3413 distinguishes a notification originator from request/response command applications.
RFC 3414 defines SNMPv3 USM identity, authentication, privacy and replay/timeliness properties, so v3 evidence must include the approved security profile rather than community-based v2c.
ED-31 preserves actual WebUI display evidence and ED-36 permits receiver/MIB/event/profile values as execution-readiness inputs.

test_case.test_name: Verify BMC SNMPv1 and SNMPv3 trap delivery as separate checkpoints
test_case.purpose: For each source-required mode, verify the actual BMC WebUI configuration is correct and one approved, non-destructive event causes an asynchronous notification to the designated receiver with the vendor-authoritative OID/varbind content, source identity, security properties and timing.
required_package: BMC firmware SNMP capability document and matching vendor MIB/trap catalog
Isolated management network and approved receiver address/port/ACL with synchronized time
Separate v1 community and v3 engine/user/security-level/auth/privacy profiles, handled outside logs/CLI
Vendor `send test trap` action or another project-approved reversible stimulus plus expected OID/varbind/severity/latency contract
Configuration backup, restore and destination-removal procedure
test_case.test_command: Run two independent checkpoints: v1, then v3. For each, operator backs up the current SNMP configuration, uses the actual WebUI to configure only the approved mode and receiver, and confirms displayed values. Start a version-specific receiver using a protected configuration file, record an empty baseline window, invoke exactly one approved safe test-notification stimulus, then correlate the received source, version, timestamp, enterprise/trap OID and every required varbind with the vendor MIB/event record. Restore configuration and remove test secrets/destination before the next mode. Do not use `snmpget -v2c` as trap proof.
test_case.expected_result: In both v1 and v3 checkpoints, WebUI shows the intended redacted configuration; exactly the expected notification arrives from the BMC within the project latency/duplicate limits and decodes against the approved MIB. v1 fields match the approved enterprise/generic/specific/varbind contract. v3 matches the approved engine/user/security level and authenticates/decrypts without replay/timeliness error. No unapproved destination receives traffic, and restore is exact.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires separate v1 and v3 evidence; success in one cannot satisfy the other. Each requires an actual asynchronous receiver record correlated to the approved stimulus and exact vendor MIB expectation, plus visual configuration and cleanup. FAIL covers absent/late/duplicate or malformed notification, wrong source/version/OID/varbind/security, secret exposure, unexpected receiver, or restore failure. If policy prohibits v1, only an authoritative Project SPEC may mark that checkpoint N/A; it is not silently replaced by v2c.
safety_gate: Use only a vendor/project-approved non-destructive test event; never invent a hardware fault or RAS injection
Keep community/auth/privacy secrets in protected receiver/BMC stores and redact all evidence
Isolate receiver and restrict destination/ACL; snapshot configuration before change
Do not confuse GET/WALK reachability with trap delivery and do not automatically retry unexpected traffic
Restore the original SNMP configuration and remove temporary destinations/secrets unless retention is explicitly approved
expected_evidence: BMC model/firmware, MIB/catalog revision and approved per-mode matrix
Before/during/after WebUI screenshots with secrets redacted
Receiver identity/tool version/time baseline and decoded raw notification for each mode
Stimulus record plus exact OID/varbind/severity/timing/duplicate comparison
Configuration diff/restore, destination cleanup and secret-redaction audit
test_case.recovery: On wrong destination, payload, authentication or secret exposure, stop the receiver/test, preserve redacted evidence, isolate the test route if needed and restore the pre-test SNMP configuration through the vendor path. Escalate before generating another event; no automatic retry.

source_conflict.preserved_original_conflict: Master procedure observes only WebUI while the title says Trap; DeepSeek substitutes v2c GET for source-required v1/v3.
source_conflict.resolution: WebUI remains required configuration evidence, but actual v1 and v3 receiver captures independently prove the title; v2c GET is explicitly non-qualifying.

blocked.reason: Standards define the notification semantics and a safe parameterized method exists; vendor MIB/event and site security values are readiness inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Vendor MIB/trap catalog, safe stimulus, receiver/network, v1/v3 profiles, latency/duplicate limits and rollback.
